preamble.summary: Psalm 123 (MT) / Psalm 122 (LXX) is the fourth Song of Ascents — a short (4-verse) eyes-lifted-to-heaven prayer for mercy. The psalm's central image — servants-looking-to-their-master's-hand — captures the humble-attentiveness posture of the dependent-pilgrim.
preamble.notable_variants: 123:1 'to you I lift up my eyes' attentive-waiting posture; 123:2 'as the eyes of servants … look to the hand of their master' as servant-dependency image; the brevity-and-urgency characteristic of Songs of Ascents.
preamble.structural_notes: MT Ps 123 = LXX Ps 122. 4 verses. Fourth Song of Ascents.

variant_notes: 'To you I lift up my eyes, O you who are enthroned in the heavens!' tracks MT. LIFT-EYES-TO-HEAVEN (not to hills, as Ps 121) — the gaze-ascends-past-creation-to-Creator.

'Behold, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master, as the eyes of a maidservant to the hand of her mistress, so our eyes look to the LORD our God, till he has mercy upon us' tracks MT. SERVANTS'-EYES-TO-MASTER'S-HAND. The attentive-dependency image: servants wait for the master's-signaling-hand. The parallel-structure includes female-servant (maidservant-to-mistress) giving both-genders equal covenant-identity.
'Have mercy upon us, O LORD, have mercy upon us, for we have had more than enough of contempt' tracks MT. DOUBLE-MERCY petition — the intensity. KYRIE ELEISON echoes.
'Our soul has had more than enough of the scorn of those who are at ease, of the contempt of the proud' tracks MT.
